chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who became junub during the month of Ramadan and forgot to perform ghusl until the month of Ramadan had passed. He said: 'He must make up the prayer and the fasting.'

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became junub (entered state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who delays ghusl until after Ramadan ends?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that delaying *ghusl* until after Ramadan does not invalidate the fast itself, but rather creates a dual obligation to make up both the missed prayers and the missed fasting days. This ruling highlights the distinct legal statuses of prayer and fasting in Shia jurisprudence, where the state of *janabah* primarily affects the validity of prayer unless one is in a state of continuous impurity that prevents performance, while the fast remains valid provided the *niyyah* (intention) was made before dawn. The emphasis on making up both acts underscores the importance of timely ritual purification to maintain the integrity of daily worship during the holy month.
